title: DVT and PE: acute, chronic or history
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's deep vein thrombosis or pulmonary embolism (only that code).
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for DVT.

HPI
Pt is a 56 y/o female presenting for f/u of acute deep vein thrombosis of the right femoral vein. Diagnosis made via ultrasound 3 weeks ago. Pt currently in the first months of anticoagulant treatment. Denies calf pain, swelling, or shortness of breath since starting meds. Tolerating therapy well. No bleeding episodes reported.

Medication List
Rivaroxaban 20mg daily.

Exam
Gen: Well-appearing, in no acute distress.
CV: RRR, CTAB.
Resp: Clear, no wheezes.
Ext: Right lower extremity shows mild swelling compared to other side. No erythema or warmth noted. Distal pulses palpable.

Assessment
1. Acute DVT of the right femoral vein. Pt is stable on current anticoagulation.

Plan
1. Continue Rivaroxaban as prescribed.
2. Continue monitoring for any signs of bleeding or worsening symptoms.
3. F/u in 4 weeks for re-evaluation.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, MD
05/14/2026
explanations: Acute DVT of the right femoral vein, still under initial treatment: I82.411 (HCC 267).
